claims.statement: The proposed paid unit is a permitted cohort-access or derived-data license tied to a validation milestone; no price, cycle time, or developer loss estimate is yet evidenced.
IVD and health-technology developers must generate performance evidence and are plausible validation-budget payers, but no target customer commitment exists.
The founder can control only a prospectively contracted, consent-governed panel and compliant processing workflow; no participant, specimen, clinic, or health-data right exists today.

EHDS creates structured secondary-use access with permits and secure environments, while IVDR requires scientific validity and analytical and clinical performance evidence; exact commercial use and national implementation remain case-specific.

commercial_mechanics.budget_owner: Clinical validation, biomarker, data science, regulatory, or research-program lead
commercial_mechanics.bundling_resistance: Specialize in fast recontact and prospective measurement for narrowly defined phenotypes that static retrospective datasets cannot answer
commercial_mechanics.customer_relationship_owner: Unknown until direct participant and institutional agreements exist; no present panel is controlled
commercial_mechanics.distribution_origin: CRO, laboratory, research-institution, and regulatory-consultant referrals

fully_loaded_economics.acquisition_cost: Participant recruitment and B2B study acquisition; both are likely material before reuse emerges
fully_loaded_economics.cash_conversion: Study deposit before recruitment, milestone billing, and final acceptance; restricted study funds are not general operating cash
fully_loaded_economics.contribution_margin: Unvalidated target 35-60% after participant, laboratory, secure-environment, governance, and channel costs
fully_loaded_economics.delivery_and_support_costs: Cohort operations, consent support, data curation, query handling, and audit-ready provenance
fully_loaded_economics.overhead_and_compliance: Data protection, ethics, security, legal governance, insurance, scientific oversight, and potential health-data permit fees
fully_loaded_economics.revenue_basis: Hypothesis: 30000-150000 PLN per protocol-specific cohort access or derived-data license, plus per-participant collection costs
fully_loaded_economics.variable_costs: Participant compensation, clinical or lab collection, specimen shipping and storage, secure processing, ethics administration, and customer-specific analysis

commercial_mechanics.likely_incumbent_response: CROs, biobanks, hospitals, laboratories, and EHDS data-access bodies can offer larger cohorts and established governance
commercial_mechanics.paid_event_or_measurable_loss: Paid event is an executed, lawful research-access or derived-data license plus delivery of a cohort milestone; measurable loss is validation delay or a failed study caused by inadequate cohort fit or data provenance
commercial_mechanics.payer: IVD manufacturer, pharmaceutical or biotechnology sponsor, digital-health company, or health-AI developer
commercial_mechanics.purchase_trigger: A model, assay, or biomarker reaches an external-validation, subgroup, post-market, or protocol-amendment gate
commercial_mechanics.renewal_event: New model version, biomarker panel, indication, subgroup, follow-up interval, or protocol creates another licensed use

contrary_evidence: EHDS and established biobanks may make much larger governed datasets available without a small private panel.
Consent withdrawal, rare phenotypes, and protocol changes may prevent reusable licensing economics.

critical_control_point.acquisition_instrument: Proposed versioned consent and data-rights agreement paired with protocol, ethics, processor, and secure-environment terms for each use
critical_control_point.counterparty_refusal_fallback: Recruit a different consenting cohort, use anonymous or permitted public data, or decline the study rather than stretch a prior consent
critical_control_point.current_owner: Participants retain applicable rights; clinics, laboratories, and institutions may control source records or specimens
critical_control_point.customer_relationship_owner: Unknown until direct participant and institutional agreements exist; no present panel is controlled
critical_control_point.duration: Consent-governed and protocol-specific; withdrawal and statutory retention rules supersede any commercial duration
critical_control_point.founder_access_description: Neuroscience and data-science expertise do not confer participant, clinical, laboratory, specimen, ethics, or health-data access rights.
critical_control_point.launch_controller: Each participant plus clinics, laboratories, ethics bodies, health-data access bodies, or sponsors as applicable
critical_control_point.renewal: New purpose or protocol requires fresh authority or confirmation under applicable governance
critical_control_point.subject: Participant relationship and protocol-specific rights to recontact, collect, process, and permit secure research use

economics.acquisition_route: CRO, laboratory, research-institution, and regulatory-consultant channels at a concrete validation gate
economics.founder_net_worth_path: A uniquely recontactable, well-governed cohort could support repeat licenses or acquisition; reaching 5m PLN likely requires several high-value panels and multi-customer reuse over 5-8 years
economics.founder_time: Up to five hours per day only with qualified clinical, laboratory, and governance partners handling regulated work
economics.gross_margin_basis: License and study fees less recruitment, participant, clinic, lab, secure-processing, governance, analysis, and channel costs
economics.payback: Target positive contribution on the first funded protocol and reuse only with lawful fresh authority; not evidenced
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 30000-150000 PLN per protocol-specific access or derived-data license plus pass-through collection costs
economics.retention_or_repeat: Repeat from follow-up intervals, new model versions, biomarkers, indications, and customer protocols

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Longitudinal recontact, consent provenance, phenotype consistency, and completed-study metadata improve cohort discoverability and reduce setup time
fingerprint.customer: IVD, digital-health, pharmaceutical, and health-AI developers needing external biomarker or model validation
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Partner with CROs, accredited laboratories, research institutions, and regulatory consultants that encounter validation gaps
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Governed participant panel with protocol-specific recruitment, secure access, and license fees for non-identifying derived datasets or permitted analyses
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Developer pays when a permitted research-access, recontact, or derived-data license is executed and the contracted cohort milestone is delivered
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A developer needs a defined phenotype cohort, additional measurements, or recontact for validation under a new protocol

founder_fit: Neuroscience and data-science background support phenotype design, provenance, and analysis-quality systems
A structured platform can reduce repeated manual study setup once governance and panel operations are established
The founder can begin with a narrow non-clinical feasibility panel and external qualified partners
B2B licensing offers scale potential without an on-camera consumer brand
risks: Sensitive health-data or specimen mishandling can cause severe participant and regulatory harm
A small cohort can be biased, underpowered, or scientifically unsuitable
Long study-sales and approval cycles can consume runway
The business cannot treat consent as irrevocable property or sell identifiable health data

structural_signature.commercial_model_descriptor: protocol specific license for secure cohort access recontact or non identifying derived data
structural_signature.control_point_descriptor: versioned consent governed engagement with a recontactable participant panel
structural_signature.critical_dependency_descriptor: participant and institutional authority for each data specimen and recontact purpose

structure.control_point: direct, consent-governed relationship with a recontactable participant panel
structure.critical_dependency: participants and data or specimen rights holders granting lawful protocol-specific use

thesis: Future operating state (2031): diagnostic and health-AI developers run rapid external validation against precisely phenotyped, recontactable cohorts rather than assembling a new study for every model update. Missing rights and coordination mechanism: ethically governed consent versioning, durable participant engagement, phenotype normalization, specimen logistics, and permitted secure research access without selling identifiable health data.
title: Recontactable Biomarker Validation Panel
uncertainties: Lawful basis, ethics route, permit needs, and secure-environment requirements for each use
Recruitment cost and retention for a sufficiently differentiated phenotype
Whether customers value recontact speed enough to pay above existing CRO or biobank options
Which outputs can be licensed without creating regulated diagnostic or medical-device claims
